s1.syndrome_frame: subacute back pain with a retroperitoneal mass
salient_findings: dull, nonradiating back pain for two months
well-circumscribed 5 cm lesion in the left retroperitoneal space
heterogeneous enhancement on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT
key_facts: 36-year-old man
two-month history of dull, nonradiating back pain
denied urinary symptoms, limb weakness, or sensory changes
unremarkable medical history, physical examination, and laboratory studies
lumbar MRI showed a lesion with low signal intensity on T1-weighted images and high signal intensity on T2-weighted images
lesion was adjacent to the iliopsoas muscle
mass was anterior to L4, abutting the left ureter and left common iliac artery
brain and chest CT scans were normal
PET-CT showed fluorodeoxyglucose avidity with an SUVmax of 5.2

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: PET-CT showed fluorodeoxyglucose avidity and a large retroperitoneal mass with heterogeneous enhancement

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Retroperitoneal location and imaging characteristics are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass is adjacent to the left ureter and left common iliac artery, and PET-CT showed fluorodeoxyglucose avidity

shortlist.label: Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Broad category that includes liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma, and the mass's imaging characteristics are consistent with a sarcoma

shortlist.label: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Location adjacent to the iliopsoas muscle and the mass's size and imaging characteristics make this a plausible diagnosis
